_readme: News archive for FootballSG. Append to items[]; never rewrite history. Every item needs a real source URL — an unsourced item must not ship. Dates must come from the article body, not a listing page: FAS listing pages mis-attribute dates. `time` is optional and Asia/Singapore — state it only when the source does; never invent one. Validated by checks/news-audit.mjs on every push.

items.title: Rafael Leão completes permanent move from AC Milan to Galatasaray
items.summary: AC Milan confirmed in an official statement on 30 August that Rafael Leão has completed a permanent transfer to Turkish side Galatasaray after seven seasons at the club, reportedly for around €38m. The Portugal winger, Serie A MVP in 2021-22, signs a four-year deal; Milan retain a 20% sell-on share of any future transfer fee.

items.title: DSA-Sec 2026 outcomes released to Secondary 1 (2027 intake) applicants
items.summary: The Direct School Admission (DSA-Sec) exercise for the 2027 Secondary 1 intake reached its outcome-notification deadline on Friday, 28 August 2026, with schools required to inform every applicant — Confirmed Offer or Wait-Listed — directly by this date, ahead of the PSLE results. DSA-Sec is the route by which schools with football talent programmes, including Singapore Sports School, select students on sporting merit, so this date matters to families who applied on a football portfolio.

items.title: 2026-27 Champions League league-phase draw held in Monaco
items.summary: UEFA held the league-phase draw for the 2026-27 Champions League at the Grimaldi Forum in Monaco on 27 August, setting the 36-team, 8-matchday league phase (144 matches total). Notable pairings include Real Madrid facing Arsenal and Inter, and holders Paris Saint-Germain drawn against Barcelona and Manchester City. The first matchday is 8-10 September 2026, with the final at the Estadio Metropolitano, Madrid, on 5 June 2027.

items.title: Gavin Lee names a 25-man Lions squad for the ASEAN Hyundai Cup 2026
items.summary: Head coach Gavin Lee confirmed the 25 players representing Singapore at the ASEAN Championship Hyundai Cup 2026, which runs from 24 July to 26 August. The Lions open their Group A campaign away to Cambodia in Phnom Penh on Friday 24 July, return home to face Timor-Leste on 27 July, then travel to defending champions Vietnam on 31 July.

items.title: Tickets released for Singapore's ASEAN Hyundai Cup home fixtures at Jalan Besar Stadium
items.summary: FAS put tickets for the Lions' home Group A fixture against Timor-Leste on sale at 11am, with tickets for the 7 August home fixture against Indonesia following on Wednesday 22 July, also at 11am. Both fixtures are at Jalan Besar Stadium.
